label: Late original-phase / <DEL> steps in sequences starting with b/h/i/u (j/m/d weaker)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase from t>=3 and at the <DEL> step (97% of activation mass; it is silent at t=0-1 and nearly silent through the copy phase). The firing rate rises with orig_idx (about 0.10 at idx 3 to 0.17 at idx 8). The strongest modulator is the first original token: if the sequence starts with b, h, i or u the rate is about 3.5x baseline, with j, m or d about 2x, and with other tokens it is low. The current input matters too: z, f, s, x, n, c and <DEL> raise the rate, and first occurrences of a token (in_first) carry 90% of the mass. The top activations (z at late positions in b/h/i-initial sequences) combine both factors. The signal looks like a graded sum of these factors, not a clean rule. first_tok in {b,h,i,u} AND in_tok in {z,f,s,x,n,c,DEL} reaches precision 0.72 but recall only 0.25, and the simple predicate gets dev F1 0.47 with mass recall 0.72. It does not fire in the copy phase after the first output, at t<2, or much on repeated tokens.
